clue.text: Drunk raved about knight, in short, supporting man in authority

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so the man comes first

parts.note: a chap is a man, a fellow

indicators.note: the curt word goes about, that is around, the jumbled letters

parts.note: speaking in short, briefly, is being terse

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering out of their order

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An intoxicated man raves at a knight while propping up some official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' scrambles raved with N into ANDVER, which 'about' wraps in the curt word. 'man in authority' looks like one phrase; the 'in' is only a link, and 'in short' belongs to the knight's phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote chapter and verse is to cite the exact source, the precise authority, for a statement.

clue.text: One 24-ing shocking result, 1-1

indicators.note: a shocking result is a jolted one, so the word's letters are shaken up

parts.note: each 1 is the Roman numeral I, so the pair gives two I letters

explanation.surface: Someone exploiting a terrible scoreline of one all.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is EXPLOIT, so 'One 24-ing' is one exploiting, someone who makes use of things. 'shocking' scrambles RESULT with two Is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who exploits a resource is a user of it, one who puts it to use.

clue.text: British isle superior to a US state

indicators.note: in a down clue superior to means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: IOW is the abbreviation for the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast

explanation.surface: A British island ranks higher than one American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: 26 15 location's vixen secures a personal loan, finally

indicators.note: secures here means holds safe within, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a vixen is a spiteful woman, which slang also calls a cow
pet works as an adjective meaning one's own special, personal (a pet project)

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A fox in a South African city underwrites a private loan in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 15 is SOUTH AFRICAN. 'vixen' suggests a fox but means an unpleasant woman, COW, which 'secures' A PET; then the last letter of loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Town is a major South African city, the country's legislative capital.

clue.text: See 13
Sound container put in order of rank

indicators.note: put in tells us one word is placed inside another

parts.note: a caste is a social rank or class
a set can be an ordered arrangement, a sequence

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange things by seniority.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a case of magnetic tape holding recorded sound or music.

clue.text: 26 15 location totally flooded, then duck under

indicators.note: in a down clue the duck goes under, so it comes after

parts.note: so wet means extremely, totally soaked
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so it gives O

explanation.surface: A South African place is completely waterlogged, so a duck dives beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Soweto is a large township of Johannesburg in South Africa.

clue.text: Historic 26 15 location's fruitlessness?

definitions.meaning: a former republic and later province of South Africa
read playfully, a condition free of oranges, without that fruit

explanation.surface: Asking whether an old South African region is barren.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Free State was a Boer republic, later a South African province, now renamed Free State.

clue.text: Action regularly applied to dish creating problem for juggler?

parts.note: hotpot is a dish of meat stewed under sliced potatoes, from Lancashire

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A recipe step that makes trouble for a circus performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire hotpot is a British stew topped with potato slices. 'regularly' takes alternate letters of Action.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for an awkward issue nobody wants to hold for long, juggled from hand to hand.

clue.text: Love finds itself in a drink knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so the letters are read from the end
in places one item inside the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink
itself refers back to love, and love is O as a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Romance turns up at the bottom of a glass that is downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itself' means love again, O, which goes in RUM; 'knocked back' reverses that, giving MOUR after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a French borrowing for love, especially a romantic affair.

clue.text: Convict held in large building for war crime

indicators.note: held in means one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
an old lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A prisoner locked up in a big edifice for wartime atrocities.
explanation.definitionFit: Plundering a captured place is looting, outlawed in war.

clue.text: Make out English service on record

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the record comes first

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Read a British naval detail from a gramophone record.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out something is to perceive or detect it, especially with difficulty.

clue.text: 26 15 location, last one to be built over river

indicators.note: over places this piece before the next one
to be built suggests these letters are put together in a new form

parts.note: the Don is a river in Yorkshire and in Russia

explanation.surface: A final structure to be erected spanning a river in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of LAST ONE gives EAST LON, followed by DON.
explanation.definitionFit: East London is a port city in South Africa's Eastern Cape.

clue.text: County with river entering city in dropping movement

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece goes inside the next

parts.note: Stoke-on-Trent is an English city, short form Stoke

explanation.surface: A county whose river flows into a city in a falling motion.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoke is the English city Stoke-on-Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: A downstroke is a downward stroke of a pen or piston, a descending motion.

clue.text: See 26
Cats listening to sharks?

indicators.note: listening to means what follows is heard, not seen on the page

parts.note: card sharks are swindlers, cheaters

explanation.surface: Felines overhearing big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheetahs are big cats, the fastest land animals.

clue.text: An earpiece — one's dropped off

definitions.meaning: a small ring worn in a newly pierced ear to keep the hole open
someone who has nodded off, a person asleep

explanation.surface: An earring has fallen out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a small hoop kept in a pierced ear, and also someone who sleeps.

clue.text: Words passed?

parts.note: a string of words, the grammatical unit, and also what a judge passes on a convict

explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is a group of words, and a judge passes sentence on the guilty.

clue.text: 26 15 location having to repair disorder

indicators.note: disorder tells us these letters are jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: A South African place needing to fix chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is South Africa's administrative capital city.

clue.text: One succeeds, finding target in range

indicators.note: in places the target inside the range

parts.note: a descant is a melody above the main tune, read here as a vocal range
an end is an aim or goal, a target

explanation.surface: Someone thrives by locating a bullseye on the shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' suggests a shooting range, but it stands for DESCANT, a high counter-melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant comes after an ancestor in the family line, succeeding them.

clue.text: Write in amount which is ejected from the mouth

definitions.text: which is ejected from the mouth

indicators.note: in places the writing inside the amount

parts.note: a sum is an amount
to put something into words is to write it

explanation.surface: Telling someone to record a figure that gets spat out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputum is saliva and phlegm coughed up and spat out.

clue.text: 26 15 location's daughter describing the place?

parts.note: urban is the adjective for a city, describing this place

explanation.surface: A South African city's girl portraying her home.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue words 'describing the place' work as a definition of an adjective: a city is urban.
explanation.definitionFit: Durban is a large port city in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal.

clue.text: Where the solution's to be placed in further education

definitions.text: Where the solution's to be placed

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Instructions on where an answer goes in a college context.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the two words, the end of further plus the first letter of education.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer goes in this very spot, the place the solver is pointing at.

clue.text: Roughly, a route taking in Quito for a start

definitions.text: Roughly, a route taking in Quito for a start

indicators.note: taking in means including another piece inside
roughly means approximately, so the letters are loosely rearranged
for a start points to the initial letter of the city name

explanation.surface: Roughly a line on the map that passes through the Ecuadorian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts Q (first letter of Quito) inside EUATOR, rearranged from A ROUTE by 'Roughly'. The whole clue describes the line, which runs just north of Quito.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary circle around the globe at zero latitude passes close to Quito, capital of Ecuador.

clue.text: Use iodine in disused land?

indicators.note: in places the element inside the land

parts.note: an ex-plot is a plot no longer used, land formerly in use
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Applying a chemical to abandoned ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disused land' is read as an EX- PLOT, a former plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, often fully or unfairly.

clue.text: 2 cut by the ear

indicators.note: playing by the ear means going by what is heard, not by spelling

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: Two people trimmed by listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things together form a couple, the number 2.

clue.text: Nationality given away with Hungarian capital a day into survey

indicators.note: into tells us the gathered pieces go inside the survey

parts.note: to scan is to survey
a secret given away is out

indicators.note: capital means the first, capital letter

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday

explanation.surface: A nationality surrendered with Budapest, one day, inside a census.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hungarian capital' suggests Budapest but means its capital letter. 'into' sends the whole gathered run inside the survey word, just after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen or native of the Republic of South Africa has this nationality.

clue.text: Record holder first after top four

indicators.note: after puts first behind the other pieces

parts.note: arch- as a prefix means chief or top, as in archbishop
IV is four in Roman numerals
1st, written IST, is short for first

explanation.surface: Getting the record after a top four finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record holder' sounds like a champion; it is someone who keeps records.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist keeps and maintains historical records and documents.
